analysis.title: The case for bonds beyond peak yields (UBS House View - Daily EMEA)
key_insights: UBS CIO rates fixed income Attractive for diversification, income and potential price appreciation. The 10-year US Treasury yield has fallen three consecutive weeks and trades below 5%, despite higher oil prices amid Middle East conflicts.

UBS says the bond market may still come under near-term pressure because the geopolitical situation is fluid, inflation has re-accelerated, hyperscalers are raising more money for AI investment, and fiscal concerns persist. It argues that forecasting the exact peak in yields matters less than investors assume over the long term.

The fall in Treasury yields suggests Treasuries are being seen as a haven asset again amid broad risk-off. Higher oil prices have put growth risks back in focus, and quality bonds should benefit if growth weakens, though this is not UBS's base case.
For capital losses to offset one year of income, 2-, 5- and 10-year Treasury yields would need to rise by about 246, 109 and 63 basis points respectively. UBS views such a move as unlikely.

The Fed is expected to hold rates this week, but markets price more tightening over the next 12 months than UBS expects. Yields may fall further as those expectations are scaled back, leaving room for capital gains in bonds.
UBS favors selective exposure to medium- and longer-duration high-quality bonds and stays cautious on the longest maturities.

The EU is considering safeguards such as quotas or tariffs on Chinese imports in chemicals, furniture and machinery, possibly presented as early as Q1 2027. The EU goods trade deficit with China reached EUR 360bn last year, and China's goods trade surplus with the EU was EUR 31.1bn in September, almost 21% higher y/y.

UBS stays Attractive on Eurozone equities and forecasts 15% earnings growth in both 2026 and 2027. It cites a manufacturing pick-up, cost discipline and higher investment in AI, electrification and defense. It favors IT, industrials, banks, consumer discretionary, health care, Germany and its European Leaders theme.

EURUSD traded at 1.117 after four straight daily declines. The DXY index rose above 102 on renewed confidence in US tech stocks. UBS sees the move as a dollar rebound, not Europe-specific stress, and expects EURUSD to recover toward 1.16 by year-end.
The French-German 10-year spread narrowed 13 basis points to about 153 basis points on Monday after Moody's maintained France's rating. UBS says it does not expect a broader European debt crisis.

tension_points.bull_case: Yields at current levels pay investors to hold duration. Fed pricing of more tightening than UBS expects leaves room for capital gains, and quality bonds hedge downside growth scenarios.
tension_points.bear_case: Bonds may face near-term pressure from fluid geopolitics, re-accelerated inflation, heavy hyperscaler borrowing for AI and fiscal concerns, and from further monetary tightening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Two-, five- and 10-year Treasury yields rising by about 246, 109 and 63 basis points respectively from current levels would offset one year of income.
